question: Can a multiscale interactive visual-analytics system make neural-network loss landscapes useful for diagnosing architectural and physics-informed-model failures?

key_findings.claim: LossLens combines global relationships among trained solutions with four local views rather than treating a single two-dimensional slice as the landscape.
key_findings.evidence: Its global graph encodes model performance, Hessian curvature, layerwise centered-kernel-alignment similarity, and pairwise mode connectivity; selecting a model opens a loss contour, Hessian view, persistence diagram, and merge tree.

key_findings.claim: Residual connections expose landscape differences that accuracy alone misses in the paper's ResNet-20 case study.
key_findings.evidence: Across four seeds per architecture on CIFAR-10, both variants reach roughly 90--92% accuracy, while the residual model has better pairwise mode connectivity, a flatter local slice, and less topological fluctuation than the no-residual model.

anchors.section: 6.1 Architecture alteration of ResNet-20 and Figure 5

key_findings.claim: The PINN case study links the harder convection coefficient to several mutually reinforcing landscape diagnostics.
key_findings.evidence: For 100 seeds at each coefficient, beta=50 has higher solution error, more dispersed solutions, weaker connectivity, a rougher local slice, and more merge-tree branches than beta=1.

key_findings.claim: The user study is formative evidence, not a controlled demonstration that LossLens improves diagnostic correctness or efficiency.
key_findings.evidence: Five experts explored the same two author-designed cases after a demonstration in a 90-minute group interview. The overall mean rating is 3.88/5, but there is no comparison group, task-accuracy endpoint, or timing baseline.

key_findings.claim: The visual encodings are sampling- and projection-dependent and costly enough to remain an offline diagnostic workflow.
key_findings.evidence: Local data take about four hours on an M1 MacBook Pro and global data about four hours on a four-A100 node for the reported cases. The authors also identify dependence on model count, parameter count, perturbation range, resolution, and visual overlap.

method.core_idea: Treat trained minima as a linked population and let analysts move between a relational overview and topological or curvature-based local diagnostics.
method.mechanism: Precompute pairwise mode-connectivity and representation-similarity measures plus per-model Hessian, two-dimensional loss slices, persistence diagrams, and merge trees; encode them in a linked React/D3 interface with filtering, selection, zoom, and pan.
assumptions: A finite set of independently trained solutions represents the relevant global landscape
The selected layer makes centered-kernel alignment a meaningful functional-similarity proxy
Random two-dimensional parameter slices preserve diagnostically important local geometry
Mode-connectivity paths and curvature correlate with trainability or failure
Analysts can correctly interpret several specialized encodings together

techniques.role: Coordinates global solution relationships with local curvature and topology views.
Measures barriers along optimized paths between trained solutions.
Places models by layerwise representation similarity.
Uses persistence diagrams and merge trees to expose minima lifetimes and branching that contours can hide.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 with versus without residual connections, four seeds each
evaluations.metric: accuracy, pairwise mode connectivity, local contour/Hessian and topological structure
evaluations.result: similar accuracy but qualitatively stronger connectivity and flatter local structure with residuals

evaluations.setting: one-dimensional convection PINNs at beta=1 and beta=50, 100 seeds each
evaluations.metric: solution error, connectivity, local roughness, persistence and merge-tree branching
evaluations.result: the beta=50 population is more erroneous, dispersed, poorly connected, sharp, and branched

evaluations.setting: 90-minute group interview with five independent experts
evaluations.metric: five-point ratings, view rankings, and free-form feedback
evaluations.result: overall mean rating 3.88 (SD 0.63); global structure view mean rank 1.75
evaluations.baseline: none; participants saw an author-led demonstration of both cases

limitations: Author-stated: metrics require long offline computation and substantial GPU memory.
Author-stated: node/edge encodings overlap as the number of trained models grows.
Author-stated: two-dimensional slices lose higher-dimensional information.
Reviewer inference: four arbitrary ResNet seeds and two curated case studies do not establish general diagnostic validity.
Reviewer inference: the group interview measures perceived usefulness after training, not diagnostic accuracy, decision quality, or time saved.
failure_modes: A chosen two-dimensional slice can look flat while an unsampled direction contains a sharp barrier.
Pairwise graph clutter and quadratic metric cost can overwhelm larger model populations.
Changing the CKA layer, landscape range, or grid resolution can reverse visual impressions.
Batch-normalization warm-up or path optimization artifacts can be mistaken for landscape structure.
Analysts may infer causal architectural explanations from correlated visual proxies.
reusable_insights: Join complementary relational, geometric, and topological summaries through linked selection instead of forcing one scalar notion of flatness.
Treat visual-analysis settings and sampling choices as first-class provenance.
A useful interface evaluation should add blinded diagnostic tasks with correctness and time endpoints.
open_questions: How stable are conclusions across random projection directions, CKA layers, path optimizers, and model samples?
Can adaptive sampling quantify uncertainty about unseen regions of the landscape?
Does LossLens improve blinded failure diagnosis compared with standard notebooks or scalar dashboards?

competitive_landscape.title: Visualizing the Loss Landscape of Neural Nets
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. introduce normalized one- and two-dimensional landscape projections for architecture and training comparisons; LossLens embeds such local slices in an interactive system with population-level connectivity and topology.

competitive_landscape.title: PyHessian: Neural Networks Through the Lens of the Hessian
competitive_landscape.difference: PyHessian provides scalable curvature statistics and architecture analyses, whereas LossLens coordinates Hessian information with contours, topology, representation similarity, and mode connectivity in an analyst-facing interface.

competitive_landscape.title: The Global Landscape of Neural Networks: An Overview
competitive_landscape.difference: Sun et al. organize theoretical and empirical evidence about global landscape geometry; LossLens operationalizes a finite-sample visual proxy for global structure rather than proving properties of the full parameter space.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: LossLens is a multiscale visual-analytics framework for explaining, diagnosing, and validating machine-learning models through their loss landscapes.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It integrates mode connectivity, CKA, performance, Hessian measures, contours, persistence diagrams, and merge trees in linked global and local views demonstrated on ResNet and PINN cases.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive contribution is the interaction design and integration of existing diagnostics, especially topology plus a population graph. Its case studies establish plausibility, but neither the finite graph nor the user interview validates general claims about the true global landscape or improved diagnosis.

reviewer_notes: Read the complete 18-page extraction, with a second pass over system encodings, both case studies, interview protocol, and limitations. Competitor records were checked against primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23. Quantitative user-study claims are descriptive because n=5 and there is no comparator.
